name: Perspective-Correct Interpolation for Projected Tetrahedra
definition: A technique to compute correct colors for triangles generated by the Projected Tetrahedra (PT) algorithm by using perspective-correct interpolation instead of the standard linear interpolation provided by graphics hardware, which causes artifacts in perspective projections.
summary: Perspective-Correct Interpolation for Projected Tetrahedra decomposes tetrahedra in object space to enable manual perspective correction in the fragment shader, avoiding depth-dependent distortions inherent in standard rasterization.
